newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain farmers say strike losses 20 bln ptas so far.
newsitem.headline: Spain farmers say strike losses 20 bln ptas so far.

text.p: Spain's agriculture sector has lost about 20 billion pesetas so far in a nine-day-old truckers strike, the farmers' cooperative CCAE estimated on Friday.
"What's obviously been most affected has been perishable goods -- milk, a lot of which has had to be thrown away -- meat and vegetables," a spokesman told Reuters.
The truck stoppage has throttled roads in almost all of northern Spain, cutting off supplies to many areas and forcing factories to shut. Among the strikers' demands are improved labour conditions.
The problem appeared to be escalating on Friday with truckers blocking many major roads.

The CCAE spokesman said the strike had affected the whole country and there now were difficulties getting citrus fruits to major Spanish cities for home consumption as well as sending goods for export.
"Almeria is the main fruit and vegetable-growing region, and it's a long way from Madrid, Bilbao and Barcelona," he said.
"It's becoming impossible to send cattle feed to farms, or commodities to factories."
But a cereal trader in the north said the the strike would not start to have a big effect unless it lasted until next week.

"So far the impact hasn't been that big, simply because people were anticipating trouble and had stocked up. Export/import loading in Catalonia has been slowed up. But transport to nearby places hasn't been too bad," he said.
Maize and sorghum, both imported into Spain, were being delayed, he added.
An agriculture ministry spokesman said he preferred not to make evaluations on the effect of the strike until it becomes clearer how long it might last.
Government officials were meeting on Friday morning to discuss the effects of the transport stoppage, he said.
